"I take this root of goodness and merit and bestow it upon all bodhisattvas, so that this merit may flow back to all bodhisattvas living in the household life, causing them all to be fully endowed with this Dharma just as the Tathāgata is;

and so that bodhisattvas who have gone forth may obtain the precepts and wisdom to be fully endowed with this Dharma, and I pray that these bodhisattvas who have gone forth may attain the precepts and wisdom just like the Tathāgata."
"So be it, World-Honored One!
How does a lay bodhisattva, while residing at home, train to fulfill the precepts of one who has gone forth?
The Buddha told the householder:
“A lay bodhisattva gives all things in charity, cherishing nothing;
their mind is always intent upon the Mahāyāna, without expectation of reward.
Furthermore, householder!
"A householder bodhisattva should purely cultivate the brahma-faring; their mind shall not even think of practicing sexual desire, much less engage in it.

Furthermore, Elder, a householder bodhisattva understands the matter of emptiness and enters the four dhyānas; through the practice of skillful means, they seek that which has no reliance, causing their will to be set upon nirvāṇa."
"Furthermore, householder!

A lay bodhisattva should practice great diligence, liberation through wisdom, and the perfections; relying upon great compassion toward all, they should receive all dharmas and protect them, teaching and transforming others by means of the Dharma."
"These are the four practices by which a householder bodhisattva, while living at home, establishes the monastic precepts.
At that time, the elder Ugga addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

Standing alone upon the ground of the household life, I shall abide by the teachings and precepts of the Tathāgata; I shall extensively realize the Buddha-way for the sake of the Tathāgata, and I shall likewise study this dharma of renunciation and further practice these prohibitions of the Dharma.
At that time, the Buddha smiled.

It is the law of all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, that when they smile, immeasurable colors, various colors, and inconceivable colors issue from their mouths, illuminating countless Buddha-lands. These rays extend upward as far as the Brahma Heaven, then return to encircle the Buddha’s body before vanishing suddenly at the crown of his head.
The worthy Ānanda rose from his seat and addressed the Buddha, saying, “The Buddha does not smile without cause; I pray that you will explain its meaning.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Ānanda, do you see how the householder Ugga makes offerings to the Tathāgata out of respect for the Dharma, and furthermore utters this lion’s roar?
Ānanda replied,
“Indeed, World-Honored One!”
"I have now seen it," [Ānanda] said. The Buddha said, "Ānanda!"
This householder Upāli, while dwelling in the state of a layperson, shall make offerings to all the Tathāgatas who appear during this Bhadrakalpa and receive their teachings.
Although he resides in a household, he will be fully endowed with the precepts of one who has gone forth; at that time, he will universally proclaim the Buddha-way for the sake of all the Tathāgatas.
Thereupon, Ānanda asked the householder Ugga:
"Is living at home a source of pleasure?
Or is living at home a source of defilement?"
"Living as a householder is not equal to leaving the household life to receive the teachings of the noble sages.
Yuga replied, "Ānanda!..."
Cease, do not speak such words as these: that the noble sages are also free from defilement, possess great compassion and liberation, and do not dwell on their own peace.
The bodhisattvas endure all sufferings and do not abandon any sentient being.
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!

Although this elder Ugga dwells in the household life, he constantly maintains an impartial mind; the many people he has delivered during this Bhadrakalpa surpass those taught by hundreds of thousands of other renunciant bodhisattvas.”
Why is this so? Ānanda!
Although there may be hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas who have left the household life, their virtue and wisdom do not equal that of the elder Ugga.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"What is the name of this sutra?
How should its name be upheld?"
The Buddha said, “Ānanda!

This sutra is, first, to be known as ‘The Questions of the Householder Ugga’; you should uphold it. Second, it is called ‘The Chapter on the Householder and the Renunciant’; third, it is called ‘Maintaining Single-mindedness in Seated Meditation and the Fame of Its Virtue.’”
The Buddha said,

“Ānanda! If there is a bodhisattva who hears this sutra as being complete in all dharmas, it is superior to the practice of pure brahmacarya for a hundred kalpas that is characterized by indolence and negligence.”
Therefore, Ānanda!

Those who wish to practice great diligence, those who wish to teach others diligence, those who wish to abide themselves in the virtues of all dharmas, and those who wish to establish all others in the virtues of the Dharma, should hear this sutra, receive and uphold it, and recite it.
Why is this? Because one who wishes to fulfill all dharmas should regard this sūtra-dharma as equal to the Tathāgata. Ānanda!
Any bodhisattva who distances themselves from this sutra distances themselves from all buddhas and shall no longer be able to see any buddhas. Why is this?
Whoever speaks this sutra shall be face-to-face with all Buddhas. Ānanda!

Even if this trichiliocosm were filled with fire, a bodhisattva should enter through it to seek to hear this Dharma, receive, uphold, recite, and chant it; they should fill the trichiliocosm with various jewels to make offerings to their teacher, receiving, upholding, reciting, and reading this sutra-dharma.

“Ānanda! If there were a bodhisattva who made offerings to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present, and having made such offerings to those Buddhas for as long as his life lasted, did not receive this sutra-dharma, was unable to recite it, and did not perform any meritorious deeds therein, he would be failing to make offerings to the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.”

Ānanda! If there should be another person who hears this sutra, receives and upholds it, recites it, and explains it extensively for others, performing various meritorious deeds therein, they have thereby made offerings to the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
"Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas take the Dharma as supreme; they are born from the Dharma.

When the Buddha had spoken thus, the Venerable Ānanda, the householder Ugga, the devas, the asuras, and the people of the world rejoiced upon hearing the sutra. They all came forward to pay homage to the Buddha and departed.
The Sūtra on the Questions of Ugra (Ugraparipṛcchā) Concerning the Practice of a Bodhisattva.
